Class ItemPicker

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.ItemPicker
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public class ItemPicker extends AbstractPanelElement
A setting whose value is an item, or a list of items: slots showing the items the setting is about, and a lens onto them. Clicking a slot opens a dialog over the screen to choose and edit them. Made for settings pages. 
// One item, the kind only (the 6.1.0 shape).
ItemPicker.builder()
        .state(() -> config.lockedItem(), config::setLockedItem)
        .build();

// A list of exact stacks.
ItemPicker.builder()
        .stacks(() -> config.kit, kit -> config.kit = kit)
        .match(ItemMatch.Match.EXACT)
        .build();

The value

Always full stacks, the consumer's, read every frame and written on every change:
  • state(Supplier<Item>, Consumer<Item>): one item, the kind only (ItemMatch.Match.ITEM); Items.AIR is none. The 6.1.0 lens, kept.
  • stack(get, set): one ItemStack; ItemStack.EMPTY is none.
  • stacks(get, set): a List<ItemStack>, in the player's order, with no empty entries.
  • rule(get, set) and rules(get, set): the same with each slot's ItemMatch, a stack and its own match mode. Needed when the player chooses the match (ItemPicker.Builder.playerChoosesMatch).
Test a stack in play against the value with ItemMatch, never with a comparison of your own: rule.matches(stack), or ItemMatch.matches(config.stack, ItemMatch.Match.EXACT, stack).

The match mode

ItemPicker.Builder.match declares how the setting compares stacks (ItemMatch has the rules). ItemMatch.Match.ITEM (the default) keeps the kind of item only: the dialog has no Edit tab and no counts. ItemMatch.Match.EXACT and ItemMatch.Match.CONTAINS keep the whole stack, and the dialog's Edit tab edits it. With ItemPicker.Builder.playerChoosesMatch the player picks, per slot, between "Any <item>" (CONTAINS) and "Exactly this" (EXACT); the declared mode is a new slot's.

ItemPicker.Builder.ignoring(DataComponentType...) and ItemPicker.Builder.ignoringCount() declare once what the setting leaves out of the comparison (ItemMatch.ignoring(DataComponentType...)): every rule the picker writes carries it, so rule.matches(stack) honors it, and with ignoringCount the Edit tab has no count. A stack or stacks lens stores plain stacks, so test those with a rule that ignores the same: new ItemMatch(stack, EXACT).ignoring(DataComponents.DAMAGE).matches(candidate).

On the page

One slot, or for a list a wrapping row of slots in order, ItemPicker.Builder.columns to a row, with an empty slot marked with a plus at the end to add one. Each filled slot has a small remove button in its top-right corner ("Remove"): a click on it, or a right click anywhere on the slot, empties it, and a list drops it, the items after it moving up one in their order. Left click anywhere else on a slot (or Enter on the focused picker) opens the dialog at that slot. Hovered, a slot shows the item's own tooltip, unless the builder gives a tooltip.

The dialog

A modal dialog of the screen, in its kind, laid out as every MenuKit dialog (equal margins, Cancel and Done centered, as tall as the shown tab):
  • The slot row at the top: the setting's slots (a list's wrapped, with an empty one at the end to add to). A click on a slot selects it, outlined; the grid fills it and the Edit tab edits it. Each filled slot has the same remove button as on the page: it empties the slot, and a list drops it, the ones after it moving left.
  • Search, the default tab: a search box, focused so typing starts at once, over a grid of every item from the creative inventory's search tab, so each variant (potions, tipped arrows, enchanted book levels, goat horns, firework durations, ominous bottles) is its own entry. A click on an entry puts one of it straight into the selected slot, replacing what was there; the slot stays selected. Enter in the search box puts the first match in the same way.
  • Edit, for EXACT and CONTAINS: the selected slot's name, count, enchantments (under "Added" those on the item, under "Not Added" those that fit it, up to their highest level, the ones a chosen enchantment excludes grayed; none for an item nothing enchants; an enchanted book's stored ones), every other component as text in vanilla's /give syntax (read by vanilla's own item parser, its errors shown as a command's), and the match choice when the player has one.
Changes are written as they are made; Done keeps them, Cancel and Escape write back the value from before the dialog opened.

A setting value, never a player's item

Nothing here touches the player's inventory, a menu or the container behind a screen, and nothing is sent to the server: the slots are not real slots, and every stack is a picture of a value.

Each slot is 18 x 18, vanilla's slot size, MenuKit's recessed slot in the Panel look and vanilla's slot sprite in the Default look.
